summary: Traffic diverted to standby variant causing long-tail latency and intermittent 504s for enterprise billing service
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 10:20 UTC NimbusFinance reported elevated end-to-end latency and intermittent 504s on their nightly billing job. Impact: 30% of billing requests experienced >5s latency and ~6% returned 504s over a 2 hour window, causing downstream reconciliation failures and customer alerts. Environment: Dedicated tenant (NimbusFinance) on prod-us-east, routing policy: cost-aware primary->standby diversion enabled for load smoothing. Observed behavior: Traffic was routed to "standby" variant replicas that reported as READY but were still performing model KV population and kernel JIT; this produced serial warmups and long-tail p99. The issue appears tied to a routing decision that prefers standby racks when observed primary CPU pressure exceeded a small threshold.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use NimbusFinance test workload (billing-batch v2) against dedicated stack in prod-us-east during peak ingestion.
2) Configure routing policy to enable standby diversion with least-cost preference.
3) Generate sustained 1200 RPS for 30 minutes; watch routing decisions in the console.
4) Observe that new connections are sent to standby replicas which report Healthy but have model cache miss rates >95% and token generation latencies rising over time.
Expected: standby replicas should be warm or traffic should not be diverted until KV/embeddings warmed.
Actual: requests see high p95/p99 and intermittent 504s due to request timeouts while replicas finish initialization.

Relevant dashboards: latency by route, replica-init-time, kv-cache-miss-rate (links in comments).
comments:
Support (2026-03-13 10:40 UTC): Confirmed increased p99 on NimbusFinance billing route. Temporarily increased route timeout to 35s to reduce 504s.
SRE Oncall (Jordan Blake, 2026-03-13 11:05 UTC): Investigating routing decisions and replica health gating. Found standby replicas reported READY earlier than KV warm complete.
Customer (NimbusFinance, 2026-03-13 11:20 UTC): Billing job failed mid-run; asks for ETA and workaround to prevent future disruptions.
Support (2026-03-13 11:45 UTC): Pinning customer to primary model variant and disabling standby diversion for the tenant. Immediate customer impact reduced; p99 returned to baseline within 8 minutes.
SRE (2026-03-13 12:10 UTC): Rolled back the recent routing policy change that expanded least-cost diversion; adding a temporary guard to prevent diversion to replicas with kv_warm=false.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Routing policy change (rolled three days ago) added cost-preference weight that allowed traffic to be sent to standby racks during brief primary pressure. Standby replicas are considered HEALTHY after container readiness but before model KV/embeddings are populated; they therefore accepted traffic too early.
Observations:
- Replica readiness probe checks only container and GPU driver; it does not include model kv/embedding warm completion.
- KV population times spiked for gptx-13b-q4o on standby racks (4-6s per shard) due to cache eviction and simultaneous preempted background IO.
- Autoscaler created standby replicas with delayed prefetch because autoscaler prioritized instance spin-up over model prewarm.
- Traffic diversion happened in bursts; serial warmups created thundering behavior as more requests hit the same initializing replicas.
Evidence: traces (trace IDs: trc-7a2b, trc-7a2c), dashboard snapshots attached to confluence page.
Risk factors: other dedicated tenants with cost-aware diversion enabled may see recurrence under load.
Open question: Why did standby kv init times increase for gptx-13b-q4o? Possibly related to kernel JIT heating between quantized kernels or NVM bandwidth contention on the rack.
resolution_notes:
Immediate mitigation applied (2026-03-13 11:50 UTC):
- Disabled cost-aware diversion for NimbusFinance tenant and pinned traffic to primary replicas.
- Increased request timeout temporarily to limit 504s during in-flight warmups.
- Manually triggered prewarm on standby replicas (kv_prefetch for affected models) to bring them to warm state.
Permanent fixes planned:
1) Change readiness gating so that replicas only report READY after model KV/embedding prefetch completes.
2) Update routing policy to consult replica kv_warm and steady-state token latency metrics before diverting traffic.
3) Add synthetic canary that exercises model init under rollout to detect long init times.
4) Tweak autoscaler to ensure prewarm completes before accepting diversion traffic (add prewarm window).
Follow-up tasks created and linked to INT tickets for implementation. Customer notified and provided a post-incident runbook.
follow_up_tasks:
- INT-4210: Implement kv_warm readiness probe in serving-runtime (owner: Jordan)
- INT-4234: Change routing policy to include kv_warm and recent-latency signals before diversion (owner: SRE)
- INT-4299: Add canary for standby warm path during canary and rollout processes (owner: DX)
- DOC-118: Update runbook and customer-facing KB on dedicated standby diversion behavior (owner: Support)
- Monitor: Add alert when >5% of diverted requests hit replicas with kv_warm=false for >5m
customer_communication:
2026-03-13 12:00 UTC - Support message to NimbusFinance: We identified the cause as premature diversion to standby replicas that were not fully warmed. We pinned your traffic to the warm primary and manually prewarmed standby replicas; you should see normal job success for subsequent runs. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and timeline when remediation is complete.
2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - Customer accepted temporary mitigation and requested ETA on permanent fix; SRE committed to INT tickets and an ETA of 2 weeks for readiness gating change.
